business_problem: The PGA TOUR wanted to give fans real-time insight into tournament outcomes, but doing so required a machine learning model that could run thousands of simulations and process nearly four billion records fast enough for live event coverage.
solution_summary: The PGA TOUR built its Win, Cut Probability model on AWS to calculate a player’s chances of advancing in and winning a tournament while tournaments are in progress. The solution uses Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate to run thousands of simulations without managing infrastructure, then relies on Amazon Redshift and Amazon DynamoDB to support analytical and low-latency application workloads behind the fan experience. This serverless architecture lets the PGA TOUR scale week to week as tournament complexity changes, keep operations lean, and deliver immersive probability insights across multiple viewing platforms.

solution_components.name: Amazon ECS
solution_components.role: Runs containerized application workloads and batch simulations.

solution_components.name: AWS Fargate
solution_components.role: Provides serverless compute capacity for containerized workloads.

solution_components.name: Amazon Redshift
solution_components.role: Stores analytical datasets and serves aggregated reporting workloads.

solution_components.name: Amazon DynamoDB
solution_components.role: Stores low-latency application, search, or telemetry state data.

data_flow: Tournament and player data feeds the Win, Cut Probability model, which runs thousands of simulations on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate and serves analytical outputs backed by Amazon Redshift and Amazon DynamoDB across PGA TOUR viewing experiences.
business_outcome: The PGA TOUR can run its model quickly, scale week to week as event complexity changes, and give audiences real-time win and cut probability insights without taking on the operational overhead of managing infrastructure.
